summary: Retested the fixes for the iteration_4 issues. Everything passed. (a) Key masking: with a valid YouTube key plus the invalid Facebook key 'FB-invalid-123' over the PUBLIC URL, start returned 200 in 3.1s. Status at t+5/10/15/20s showed live=True, platforms ['youtube'], failed_platforms ['facebook']. Log lines show 'rtmp://127.0.0.1:<port>/rtmp/***', and neither key appeared in any status response (0 leaking polls). (b) UI with the same setup: signed in via Clerk ticket, Library > Stream > Go Live. The LIVE badge appeared and data-testid='studio-failed-platforms' said 'Not live on facebook: the platform refused the stream key. Check it in Step 1.' End Stream worked and the warning went away. (c) Real Facebook stream alone (SECS=30, run twice): start 200, platforms ['facebook'], failed_platforms [] at start and on every poll, live throughout, no ffmpeg log lines, stop OK. (d) pytest /app/backend/tests: 24/24 passed. Destinations were cleared after every run, and no tee ffmpeg processes were left running.

issues: The failed-platform warning uses the raw lowercase id ('Not live on facebook'). It should show 'Facebook'.
The raw ffmpeg line ('[tee @ 0x...] Slave muxer #1 failed: Input/output error...') is shown to the user under studio-encoder-log. It is noisy and technical.
The header chips still show both YouTube and Facebook with no failed state on the Facebook chip.

action_items: Optional polish: capitalize the platform names in studio-failed-platforms, hide or simplify the raw ffmpeg log line, and mark failed platforms on the header chips.
critical_code_review_comments: streamer._drain masks keys with exact string replace per output. That is fine for the current URL format, but it would not catch URL-encoded keys.

failed-slave detection depends on the ffmpeg tee message text 'Slave muxer #N failed' and on tee indices matching the order of session.outputs. That is correct today, but it is fragile across ffmpeg versions.
Carried over: relay.handle swallows upstream errors silently; friendly_error has a broad 'Connection' match; the stream key is visible in the ffmpeg argv of the relay path only (local URL).
